title: Eating out with friends and family without ruining your progress
intro: You don't need to turn down food invitations to lose fat. With a little strategy on your plate and in your glass, you can lepak, enjoy good food and still keep progressing.

sections.p: What matters is your weekly average, not one night. If you eat balanced 80% of the time, one big meal with friends can still fit. The next day, go back to your usual routine.

sections.h: Arrange your plate the easy way
sections.p: At a nasi campur stall, fill half your plate with vegetables. Take one protein like chicken, fish or eggs, and one scoop of rice. Ask for less gravy or put it on the side.

A glass of teh tarik can be an estimated 150 to 200 kcal, and it's easy to add a second glass while chatting. Try teh o kosong, less sweet, or warm water. If you want a sweet drink, choose one and enjoy it slowly.
At the mamak or a restaurant, share desserts or fried dishes with friends. Put your spoon down for a while as you chat. Usually you'll feel full sooner.

When your mum or makcik urges you to take more, try saying 'It's really delicious, I'm full already, can I tapau a bit for later?' Smile and say thank you. You don't need to explain your diet to everyone.

action: Before going out, eat a small protein snack like a boiled egg so you're not too hungry.
Switch one sweet drink to teh o kosong or warm water this week.
Use the half-plate vegetable formula every time you eat nasi campur.
Pick one 'must-have' food when eating out, and enjoy it without guilt.
myth: Many think that after eating a lot at a buffet, it's better to skip meals the next day to 'make up for it'. Actually, skipping meals often makes you hungrier and leads to overeating again, so just continue eating normally the next day.

faq.q: What are lighter options at the mamak?
faq.a: Try roti telur or chapati with dhal, tandoori chicken, or plain rice with grilled lauk and vegetables. One plain roti canai, an estimated 300 kcal, can still be eaten, just watch the amount and the gravy.

faq.q: My weight went up the morning after a big meal. Is it ruined?
faq.a: Usually that's water and salt, not fat. Salty and carb-heavy food makes your body hold water temporarily. It usually goes back down in 2 to 3 days if you return to your routine.

faq.q: How often can I eat out when trying to lose fat?
faq.a: There's no fixed number. Many people can still eat out 2 to 3 times a week with smart choices. Watch your progress over 2 to 3 weeks and adjust as needed.
